Subject: Sessionized peak vs basal throughput — post-call clarifications

Thanks again for the call earlier — great context on the personalization pilot. I wanted to capture a short recap + concrete asks so our infra/ops folks can size properly. TL;DR: we need the session characteristics and a short traffic sample to turn your peak/steady numbers into a tokens/sec sizing and a recommended slot plan.

Recap from call (high level):
- Endpoint: /v1/personalize/cart (interactive personalization + streaming autocomplete)
- Target SLOs discussed: 95th latency <= 300ms for non-streaming responses; streaming partials acceptable with per-token latency under ~80ms for a good UX
- Pilot traffic: baseline intermittent QPS, with short sharp peaks during browsing spikes (promo bursts)

Concrete asks (to size throughput / concurrency):
1) 7-day sample: a CSV or JSON sample with timestamped request counts (1-min resolution), per-request token counts (input+output), and a session id when available (we referenced fg_traffic_snapshot.csv on the call).
2) Session distribution: percentiles for session length (minutes), requests per session, and percent of sessions that require streaming (autocomplete vs full generation).
3) Peak window characterization: how long are your 95th-percentile peaks (e.g., 1–3 minutes, sustained 10+ minutes)? This matters because we recommend different headroom for short crests vs sustained surge.
4) Any hard latency must-haves for streaming (per-token render deadlines) and tolerable fallback behavior (e.g., downgrade to shorter completions or cached baseline).

Quick numbers I sketched on the call — please confirm or correct:
- Steady QPS: ~15 qps overall (all regions)
- Peak QPS: ~150 qps for cart-personalize during promo events
- Median tokens/request (input+output): ~600 tokens (varies by template)
- Estimated peak tokens/sec (naive): 150 QPS * 600 tokens = 90,000 tokens/sec (we'll refine once we see per-request timing)

Attachments: fg_payload_example.json (sample payload we used in the demo), slo_matrix.xlsx (template for mapping latency/availability requirements).

Next steps I propose:
- You: drop the 7-day trace + session distribution (attach to this thread or share a Drive link)
- Us: Karthik and Ben will produce a short pilot sizing note (tokens/sec, slot count, streaming slot config) within 48 hours of receiving the trace
- Schedule follow-up: 30m on Wed/Thu next week to review sizing and handback. If either of those times don't work, propose alternatives.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Soojin

- 7-day sample: attached (1-min buckets, redacted user ids) — you should see two larger promo crests on Tue/Thu (each ~4–6 mins) and several smaller spikes.
- Session distribution (from our telemetry): median session length = 6.8 minutes, 75th = 11m, 95th = 28m. Requests per session median = 18, 95th = 72.
- Streaming: ~40% of sessions trigger streaming autocomplete (partial tokens returned as user types); when streaming, average generation rate is ~45 tokens/sec and typical completion lengths range 40–250 tokens for autocomplete flows. Full generation (non-streaming) average output length ~420 tokens.
- Peak windows: our promo crests tend to be short (3–8 mins at 90–160 QPS), occasional sustained traffic for up to 30m during marketing pushes.

Couple of clarifying Qs for sizing:
1) Do you need the per-session KV cache to be persisted for the full session (>30m) or can we accept evictions and rebuilds for long tails?
2) For streaming slots: can Redwood support per-session multiplexing (1 slot can serve N concurrent lightweight streams) or do you size 1:1 slot to active stream?

If helpful I can also share a redacted 1-hour trace with full per-request token counts (I left it off the CSV to keep the file small).

Great data, Amelia — this helps a lot. A few quick notes from sizing perspective and answers to your Qs: 

1) KV cache behavior: for sessionized personalization we recommend keeping the KV cache pinned for the life of the session where possible. Evictions are OK for sessions >45m, but for the 30m tails you described we would aim to keep warm. That avoids re-tokenization and reduces average token compute on replays. If preserving RAM for long tails is a concern we can recommend a two-tier strategy (pin active sessions for 30m, soft-evict LRU beyond that).

2) Streaming multiplexing: Redwood's runtime supports multiplexing lightweight streaming consumers on a single GPU slot up to a point — it's dependent on per-token generation cost and network constraints. For planning, treat streaming slots as "weighted slots". Example calculation below.

Sizing sketch (naive, to be refined after we ingest the actual 7-day trace):
- Peak QPS: 150 qps (we'll include a 1.5x safety margin for headroom => plan for 225 qps peak capacity)
- Median tokens/request: we'll treat autocomplete and full-gen separately. Using your numbers: autocomplete generation ~60 tokens on average (streams), full-gen ~420 tokens. If 40% of sessions are streaming and those requests are smaller, effective average tokens/request across all traffic ~600 (your number) still holds as long-run average.
- Peak tokens/sec (plan): 225 qps * 600 tokens = 135,000 tokens/sec (this is conservative for short crests)

Streaming-specific sizing:
- You reported streaming generation rate ~45 tokens/sec. For worst-case concurrency, assume each active stream produces at 50 tokens/sec. If peak has 150 qps and 40% are streaming, that’s 60 streaming starts/sec. Average concurrent streaming sessions depends on session duration for streaming interactions (you said autocomplete interactions are short; assume 10–20s per stream event), so concurrent streams ≈ 60 * 15s = 900 active streams in a peak second.
- If we capacity each GPU slot to safely handle ~60k tokens/sec (model-dependent, quantized), then 135k tokens/sec implies ~3 slots for raw token throughput plus additional slots for multiplexed streaming concurrency headroom. For the streaming concurrency (900 concurrent 50 tps streams -> 45k tokens/sec additional pressure) we’d target an additional 1–2 slots to keep per-token latency low and avoid queueing.

Recommendation (pilot):
- Initial pilot commit: 5 slots configured with streaming-optimized kernel/profile (this provides ~300k tokens/sec nominal headroom across the fleet plus concurrency tolerance). We'll create a more exact slot-to-GPU mapping once we know model size/quantization and per-request seq lengths.
- Autoscaling: configure burst autoscale for short crests (scale up aggressively on 1–2 minute windows) with a cooldown that lets the fleet scale down only after ~10 minutes to avoid thrash during promo bursts.

I'll put together a 1-page sizing note that converts your real trace into tokens/sec, recommended slots, and initial autoscale policy. Expect that by EOD once you drop the 7-day extract.

— Karthik
